newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire calls for U.N. monitors as rebels press.
newsitem.headline: Zaire calls for U.N. monitors as rebels press.

text.p: Zaire, facing a rebel advance on its military base in Kisangani, called on Wednesday for urgent implementation of a United Nations plan calling for a ceasefire and withdrawal of foreign forces.
A government statement in the capital Kinshasa urged the United Nations to send international monitors immediately to oversee the pullout of the troops.

"The president and the government demand the deployment, without delay, of an international monitoring force to implement the peace plan of (U.N. envoy) Mohammed Sahnoun," said the statement signed by government spokesman Jean-Claude Biebie.
The force would "verify on the spot the withdrawal of all foreign forces," it added. Zaire accuses Rwanda, Uganda and Burundi of helping the rebels, a charge all three deny.

A February 18 U.N. Security Council resolution on the fighting between the Tutsi-led rebels and the Zaire army called for a truce, the pullout of all foreign troops including European mercenaries backing the army and respect for Zaire's territorial intergrity.
Zaire, which preferred a French-backed plan for a U.N. intervention force, described the resolution as timid.
African foreign ministers who met in Kinshasa last month said Zaire had insisted on the monitors as a condition for attending a summit on the crisis later this month in Kenya.
It was not clear if any agreement was reached on this in talks between Sahnoun and Zairean officials last month.
Belgium said earlier Zaire had approved the U.N. plan designed to end the crisis in its former African colony.
"We are pleased to see that Mr Kamanda has confirmed that his country has approved a five-point United Nations plan...," foreign ministry spokesman Andre Querton said.
He told reporters Belgian Foreign Minister Erik Derycke had met his Zairean counterpart Kamanda Wa Kamanda on Monday.
Querton said many African countries were interested in the initiative by U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan to try to set up an international humanitarian force.

On the battlefield, defeated Zairean soldiers surrendered their weapons to rebels in the eastern town of Kindu on Wednesday and the rebel army was reported to be closing in on the strategic northeastern capital of Kisangani.
Kindu, up the Zaire river from Kisangani, was captured by rebels on Sunday and a new administration installed.
